- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots in the next few days; apply a downward correction of 5–10% for the immediate follow-up period.
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >10% over 3–5 days), consider mean reversion bias — reduce forecast toward recent 7-day average.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; check for abrupt reversal and reduce forecast slope accordingly.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; dampen volatility in forecast curve unless sentiment is strongly sustained.
